Governance Arrangements.q: A department head questions whether the effort of maintaining a clear governance framework really pays off for a project. One of the advantages being claimed for it, however, is not something governance delivers. Which of the following is NOT a benefit of clear governance frameworks?
Governance Arrangements.w: Governance defines limits rather than granting unlimited power.

n.3: Accountability is a core outcome of good governance.
n.1: Consistency comes from defined decision paths.
n.4: Stakeholders gain confidence when governance is clear.
n.2: Governance ensures financial authority remains controlled.

Governance Arrangements.q: A newly appointed project board is defining which responsibilities fall within its remit as opposed to those handled by the project manager and delivery team during day-to-day execution. Reviewing a proposed list of activities, which of the following is NOT a role typically covered by project governance?
Governance Arrangements.w: Project scheduling is a planning activity, not a governance role.

n.4: Identifying stakeholders is part of governance stakeholder oversight.
n.3: Approving budgets is a core governance responsibility.
n.0: Ensuring quality falls under governance controls.
n.1: Overseeing deliverables is included in governance oversight.

Governance Arrangements.q: An organisation is setting up governance arrangements for its portfolio of change projects and wants to define what these arrangements should contain. A consultant is asked to identify the core components. Which of the following identifies two functions typically included in project governance arrangements?
Governance Arrangements.w: Approval processes and delegation of authority are core components of project governance.

n.4: These relate to operations or communications, not governance.
n.0: While important, these are team management tools, not governance elements.
n.3: These are financial tactics, not governance functions.
n.2: These are more aligned with corporate image than project governance.

Governance Arrangements.q: A PMO is explaining to senior managers why decision-making authority is distributed to defined levels within the governance structure rather than held centrally. One manager challenges the rationale. Which of the following is NOT a reason to establish delegated authority within project governance?
o: To reduce bottlenecks in decision making
To ensure decisions can be made at the right level
Governance Arrangements.w: Delegation reduces the need for excessive oversight by distributing authority effectively.

n.2: Delegation distributes authority, not increases oversight.
n.0: One goal of delegation is decision-making at appropriate levels.
n.1: Delegation helps define who is responsible for what.
n.3: Delegated authority assigns decision-making responsibility.

Governance Arrangements.q: After a project has formally closed and been handed over to the business, the project manager decides to take on ongoing responsibility for realising its benefits. What is the main concern with this?
o: The project manager is overstepping into sponsor-level accountability
The schedule will not be met
The team will not deliver outputs
The project will require less governance
Governance Arrangements.w: Benefits ownership typically sits with the sponsor or business, not the project manager post-delivery.

Governance Arrangements.q: Midway through a transformation project, market conditions shift and questions are raised about whether the investment is still worthwhile. The governance board looks to the sponsor for assurance. Which statement best reflects the sponsor's role in maintaining governance over project success?
o: Running the daily agile stand-ups and sprint ceremonies
Managing the delivery team's individual performance reviews and appraisals
Writing the user documentation and operating instructions manuals
Assigning and scheduling individual development tasks to team members
Ensuring the project continues to support the business case
Governance Arrangements.w: The sponsor ensures the project remains aligned with its justification throughout.

n.1: Performance reviews are handled at team lead or HR level.
n.3: Task assignment is a project manager or team lead responsibility.
n.2: User documentation is typically written by the delivery team.
n.0: Stand-ups are delivery-focused and facilitated by the scrum master or team.

Governance Arrangements.q: Following a review showing that the expected benefits have fallen substantially, the governance board decides to pause the project rather than continue. What does this decision demonstrate?
o: Effective governance decision-making based on the business case
An overreaction to relatively minor benefit changes
A sign of inadequate planning at initiation
A clear failure of project delivery performance
A fundamental lack of stakeholder support for delivery
Governance Arrangements.w: Pausing based on updated viability reflects effective governance.

Governance Arrangements.q: Midway through a warehouse automation project, the sponsor notices a major discrepancy between planned and actual expenditure and asks for evidence so corrective action can be authorised at the next board meeting. Which governance report is designed to highlight this variance?
Governance Arrangements.w: Financial status reports compare planned vs. actual costs to identify variances.

n.0: Risk reports identify potential issues, not cost variances.
n.2: Quality audits assess product standards, not finances.
n.1: Change logs track scope changes, not expenditure variances.
n.3: Registers list stakeholders, not financial data.

Governance Arrangements.q: A product owner on an agile software project is reviewing the boundaries of their remit with the project sponsor, who wants to avoid any overlap of accountabilities. Which of these activities would fall outside the governance responsibility of a product owner?
o: Representing user needs to the team
Governance Arrangements.w: Product owners do not sign off the business case — this is a sponsor/board responsibility.

n.0: Backlog prioritisation is a core product owner responsibility.
n.3: Product owners clarify acceptance with the team.
n.4: They liaise with users to gather feedback.
n.2: They act as a voice of the user throughout delivery.

Governance Arrangements.q: In a projectised organisation, a programme introduces stricter governance controls. What is the most likely consequence for decision-making authority at project level?
o: Authority shifts fully to external stakeholders
Authority is removed from the project manager entirely
Authority is constrained by additional oversight and escalation requirements
Authority remains unchanged as governance only affects reporting
Authority becomes more decentralised to team members
Governance Arrangements.w: Governance layers impose controls that constrain autonomy and require escalation, even in projectised structures.

Governance Arrangements.q: On a manufacturing project, individuals have been assigned specific tasks from the breakdown structure and report progress to their team leader. A new joiner asks how their own accountability fits into the governance structure. Which of the following best describes the responsibility of project team members?
o: To deliver work packages as assigned
Governance Arrangements.w: Team members are responsible for completing assigned work within agreed parameters.

n.2: Milestone sign-off is done at a governance level.
n.4: Only sponsors or boards authorise budget changes.
n.1: Benefit realisation is a sponsor-led activity.
n.3: Exceptions are approved by project boards or sponsors.

Governance Arrangements.q: When a serious risk emerges on a project, the project manager realises he does not know who he should escalate it to or what authority applies. There is no documented route for such situations. What governance failure does this indicate?
Governance Arrangements.w: Escalation routes are part of governance clarity.

Governance Arrangements.q: An assurance reviewer is confirming that a project's governance ensures compliance with the rules and obligations that genuinely apply to it. One listed item, however, is not something governance enforces. Governance is required to ensure compliance with all of the following EXCEPT:
Governance Arrangements.w: Decor guidelines are aesthetic and not enforced by project governance frameworks.

n.4: Statutes must be complied with under governance.
n.1: Policies ensure project alignment with organisational rules.
n.0: SOPs are part of governance documentation.
n.2: Authority delegation is central to governance structures.

Governance Arrangements.q: A long-running programme prepared a thorough business case at the outset but has not looked at it again, even as market conditions and priorities have shifted considerably. What is the main governance risk?
o: It creates unnecessary duplication of the project documentation
It weakens ongoing stakeholder engagement across the project
It may fail to reflect changing viability and context
It increases the technical complexity of the delivery work
It slows down day-to-day project delivery decisions
Governance Arrangements.w: Business cases must be reviewed to ensure ongoing justification.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project passes an initial approval but is not reassessed at stage boundaries. What is the most significant governance risk?
o: The business case may no longer reflect current viability
Stakeholder communication becomes excessive and difficult to manage
The project timeline becomes permanently fixed and inflexible
The project manager gradually loses control of delivery tasks
The suppliers gradually gain too much delivery authority
Governance Arrangements.w: Without review points, the business case is not updated, risking continuation of a non-viable project.

Governance Arrangements.q: An organisation is documenting how problems that cannot be resolved at working level are formally raised and dealt with under its governance arrangements. Complete the statement: a governance framework defines the _______ for raising and resolving project issues.
Governance Arrangements.w: The escalation process outlines how issues are formally raised and handled.

n.3: Menus are unrelated to governance processes.
n.1: Birthdays are social events, not governance topics.
n.2: Parties are informal, not process definitions.
n.0: Playlists have no place in governance frameworks.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager struggles to secure specialist resources because functional managers prioritise operational work. Which adjustment would most directly address this governance issue?
o: Redefine reporting lines to strengthen project authority within a matrix
Outsource all specialist roles to various external suppliers
Introduce more frequent project team progress review meetings
Increase the overall project budget allocation quite substantially
Extend the project timeline to relieve ongoing delivery pressure
Governance Arrangements.w: Adjusting authority structures in a matrix addresses resource control conflicts directly.

Governance Arrangements.q: A team escalates every issue directly to the sponsor rather than the project manager. What is the most likely cause?
o: The team holds an unusually high degree of delivery autonomy
The escalation process is functioning exactly as intended
The sponsor has clearly delegated decision authority to the manager
The governance framework deliberately routes issues through the sponsor
The project manager lacks clarity or credibility in their role
Governance Arrangements.w: Bypassing the project manager suggests weak authority or unclear role definition.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project is authorised largely because several comparable initiatives delivered well in previous years, with little fresh analysis of the current situation. What is the governance concern regarding the business case?
o: It omits a detailed stakeholder communication and engagement plan
It relies on assumptions rather than current justification
It overstates the available technical capability of the team
It disregards the resource and capacity constraints on delivery
It prioritises operational delivery over strategic project outcomes
Governance Arrangements.w: Business cases must be based on current context, not past assumptions alone.

Governance Arrangements.q: The governance board is presented with a project offering high potential benefits but also carrying a high level of risk to delivery. What is the most appropriate interpretation of this proposal?
o: The project can proceed without any formal governance oversight
The project may be viable if risks are understood and managed
The project is certain to succeed given its high benefits
The project should be rejected automatically because the risk is high
The project manager alone should decide whether to proceed
Governance Arrangements.w: High benefit projects can be viable if risks are acceptable and managed.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project continues because significant investment has already been made, despite poor future outlook. What bias is affecting the business case?
Governance Arrangements.w: Sunk cost bias leads to continuation despite lack of future justification.

Governance Arrangements.q: A busy executive questions why they should stay engaged as sponsor once a project is underway, rather than leaving it entirely to the project manager. What is one reason the project sponsor should remain involved throughout the project?
o: To draft the detailed delivery plans and work schedules
To manage the delivery team's day-to-day operational workload
To ensure strategic oversight and alignment with business case
To sign off each work package description and estimate
To configure and prioritise the team's sprint backlogs
Governance Arrangements.w: The sponsor owns the business case and ensures it remains valid throughout the project.

n.1: Daily workload is managed by the project manager.
n.0: Delivery planning is part of the PM’s remit.
n.3: Work packages are created and approved at a delivery level.
n.4: Sprint planning is typically agile-team specific, led by product owners or scrum masters.

Governance Arrangements.q: During delivery of a project, the project manager realises that committing to a supplier invoice would take spending beyond their agreed authority limit. In line with the governance arrangements, the next step is to:
Governance Arrangements.w: Overspend breaches governance limits and must be escalated for board approval.

n.2: Ignoring financial breach violates governance.
n.1: Parties don’t resolve authority breaches.
n.3: Rescheduling tasks doesn’t address financial breaches.
n.0: Scope changes require proper approval, not blind changes.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project moves from one phase to the next without any formal approval ever being sought at its key milestones. What does this indicate about the way its business case lifecycle is being managed?
o: Improved autonomy for the delivery team
Governance Arrangements.w: Continuation decisions should be formally reviewed and approved at defined points.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project's governance arrangements set out how much each role is allowed to commit financially without seeking approval. Complete the statement: limits of financial authority are set by delegated ___ within the governance framework.
Governance Arrangements.w: Delegated responsibilities include defined spending limits for different roles.

n.2: Procedures outline steps but don’t themselves set limits.
n.1: Policies guide behavior but don’t specify individual authority limits.
n.0: Standards set quality benchmarks, not financial limits.
n.3: Templates provide formats, not authority definitions.

Governance Arrangements.q: A software development project uses agile delivery. Who typically acts as the voice of the customer to ensure value delivery?
Governance Arrangements.w: The product owner represents stakeholders and ensures the team delivers value.

n.2: The project manager handles coordination, not stakeholder representation.
n.0: The Scrum Master facilitates process, not value direction.
n.4: The technical lead ensures technical quality, not value.
n.1: The sponsor provides oversight but not day-to-day product direction.

Governance Arrangements.q: A projectised organisation running many concurrent projects finds that specialist staff and equipment are frequently duplicated and under-used across teams. Senior management asks the PMO to identify the underlying structural cause. What is the underlying structural issue?
Governance Arrangements.w: Projectised structures can lack resource efficiency due to duplication across projects.

Governance Arrangements.q: A traditionally functional organisation creates project manager job titles but insists that departmental heads retain full control over their staff, budgets and priorities. A reviewer is asked to predict how project delivery will be affected. What outcome is most likely?
o: Limited project authority and continued functional dominance
Improved delivery speed across all projects
Governance Arrangements.w: Functional dominance persists, limiting project authority despite role introduction.

Governance Arrangements.q: A large engineering organisation retains functional departments but assigns project managers limited authority over resources. During delivery, conflicts arise over prioritisation of work. Which organisational structure is most consistent with this scenario?
o: Functional structure with no project coordination mechanisms
Weak matrix structure where functional managers dominate resource decisions
Projectised structure with full authority delegated to the project manager
Balanced matrix with equal authority between project and functional managers
Hybrid structure with rotating governance roles across departments
Governance Arrangements.w: A weak matrix is characterised by functional dominance and limited project manager authority, leading to prioritisation conflicts.

Governance Arrangements.q: A PMO is trying to roll out a single, consistent governance model across an organisation that delivers work using a mix of predictive and iterative approaches side by side. Which structure creates the greatest challenge for applying a consistent governance model across projects?
Governance Arrangements.w: Hybrid structures combine different delivery methods, making consistent governance harder to apply.

n.2: Functional structures are consistent but not project-focused.
n.3: Agile frameworks have consistent but adaptive governance.
n.0: Project-based structures apply uniform governance.
n.1: The V-model applies structured delivery with clear governance.

Governance Arrangements.q: During an approval review, a board member notes that the submitted business case sets out the costs in considerable depth but says very little about the benefits the project would deliver. What is the main weakness?
o: It focuses too heavily on delivery planning
It fails to demonstrate value and justification
Governance Arrangements.w: A business case must demonstrate value through benefits, not just costs.

Governance Arrangements.q: A PMO is documenting the differences between the various matrix arrangements used across the business so that authority is understood consistently. It wants to identify what most clearly separates a balanced matrix from a weak one. Which governance feature best differentiates a balanced matrix from a weak matrix?
o: Presence of a project manager role
Equal authority between project and functional managers
Governance Arrangements.w: Balanced matrices distribute authority equally, unlike weak matrices.

Governance Arrangements.q: When designing governance for a phased construction project, the sponsor insists the framework be tied to the stages of the life cycle. A team member asks what this alignment is intended to achieve. The governance framework should be aligned with the project's life cycle to ensure what key benefit?
o: Decisions are made at appropriate stages
Governance Arrangements.w: Aligning governance with the life cycle supports effective decision making at relevant phases.

n.2: Speed isn't the core goal—appropriate timing is.
n.0: Bonuses are unrelated to governance design.
n.3: Meeting reduction is not a direct governance goal.
n.4: Supplier payment terms are contractual, not governance-driven.

Governance Arrangements.q: A portfolio director is deciding how to distribute limited funding and specialist staff across competing initiatives, and reviews how each connects to the organisation's stated objectives. What primary benefit does linking a project to organisational objectives provide in this situation?
Governance Arrangements.w: Alignment helps leaders prioritise resources toward projects that serve strategic aims.

n.0: Décor is unrelated to strategic alignment.
n.4: Lunch duration is not a strategic benefit.
n.1: Celebrations are cultural, not strategic outcomes.
n.3: Random tasks undermine strategic focus.

Governance Arrangements.q: A significant change request has been raised that would affect the project's scope, timescale and budget, and it is unclear who should decide on it. Which responsibility is typically shared between the project manager and the sponsor?
o: Completing all individual team member performance reviews
Installing and configuring the technical tools and software
Maintaining the issue log and daily progress records
Approving changes that impact scope, time, or cost
Drafting the detailed content of each work package

n.0: Performance reviews are a line management responsibility.
n.2: The issue log is maintained by the PM or project support.
n.1: Technical setup is not a governance responsibility.

Governance Arrangements.q: A PMO is drafting the standard contents of its project governance framework and reviewing a list of candidate items, one of which is really an HR matter. Which of the following is NOT typically included in a governance framework?
Governance Arrangements.w: Holiday policies are HR-driven and not part of project governance frameworks.

n.1: Decision rights procedures are governance essentials.
n.4: Escalation paths ensure issues are escalated appropriately.
n.3: Reporting requirements enforce transparency.
n.0: Authority levels are central to delegated governance.

Governance Arrangements.q: An external regulatory audit of a completed project finds that several key documents were released without the required sign-off. The sponsor asks which governance element broke down. Which governance element failed?
Governance Arrangements.w: Approval processes define who must sign off and ensure documents are properly authorised.

n.2: Team building is an HR activity, not a governance control.
n.4: Lessons learned are retrospective reviews, not approval mechanisms.
n.3: Scheduling sets timelines, not authority for approvals.

Governance Arrangements.q: An organisation is formalising how the order and authority of project decisions are set out within its governance arrangements. Complete the statement: governance ________ define the sequence and authority for project decisions.
Governance Arrangements.w: Procedures outline the steps and authority levels for decisions in governance.

n.1: Festivities are unrelated to decision-making.
n.2: Celebrations don’t guide governance steps.
n.3: Themes are design-related, not governance frameworks.
n.0: Recipes have no role in governance.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project is delivered fully within its agreed scope, budget and schedule, yet a year later the organisation finds that the intended business benefits have not materialised. A governance review asks who is most accountable for this shortfall. Which governance role is most accountable?
Governance Arrangements.w: Sponsors are accountable for benefits realisation.

Governance Arrangements.q: During appraisal of a proposed project, stakeholders want to understand when the value it promises is likely to be realised. Which TWO factors influence the timing of value delivery in a business case?
Governance Arrangements.w: Timescale and benefit timing determine when value is realised.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager escalates a supplier dispute to the sponsor because it threatens delivery tolerances. The sponsor criticises the escalation as unnecessary detail. What is the best assessment?

The team should resolve all supplier issues without escalation
The project manager acted appropriately because tolerances were threatened
The dispute should only be reported after project closure
Escalation should be avoided unless costs have already been incurred

Governance Arrangements.q: During the initiation phase of a large infrastructure project, stakeholders question who can authorize budget changes. Which governance tool clarifies spending limits at each level?

n.3: A risk register logs risks, not financial authorities.
n.4: A communication plan defines information flow, not budget limits.
n.2: A resource histogram shows staffing levels, not spending approval.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project has a clear escalation route, but team members bypass it and raise concerns directly with senior executives. What is the most likely governance impact?
o: It removes the need for project board oversight
It improves accountability because more people are informed
It creates uncontrolled escalation and weakens agreed authority routes
It confirms the escalation route is unnecessary
It strengthens decision-making by involving senior leaders earlier
Governance Arrangements.w: Bypassing agreed escalation routes can confuse authority, distort priorities and weaken governance control.

Governance Arrangements.q: A governance review is clarifying which activities sit with the project manager as opposed to the sponsor or board. Which of the following tasks would the project manager most likely be accountable for?

Governance Arrangements.w: The project manager delivers the plan and provides regular status updates to governance bodies.

n.0: Sponsors and governance boards authorise the business case.
n.4: Benefit realisation is typically sponsor-led.
n.2: Governance strategy is a board-level responsibility.
n.3: Funding is allocated at a senior governance level, not by the PM.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project sponsor wants to change a major deliverable. Which governance element should define who has the authority to approve this change?

n.2: Resource calendars relate to availability, not approval rights.
n.1: The comms plan outlines information flow, not governance authority.
n.4: Team charters guide team dynamics, not formal approval authority.

Governance Arrangements.q: A programme director is reviewing recurring problems reported across several matrix-organised projects in order to strengthen governance. Governance Arrangements.w: Matrix structures commonly create ambiguity and conflicting priorities.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager is reviewing their remit to confirm which responsibilities genuinely sit with them and which belong to more senior governance roles. Which of these is NOT typically a responsibility of the project manager?
Governance Arrangements.w: Executive funding is a governance board or sponsor responsibility, not the PM’s.

n.3: The PM manages risks within governance thresholds.
n.4: The PM communicates with both internal and external stakeholders.
n.2: The PM ensures outputs are delivered on time and to spec.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager has been appointed to lead a major transformation and is briefed that the team will be fully assigned to the project for its duration. Which of the following is a key characteristic of a project-based organisational structure?
o: Project managers hold little authority over the assigned team
Functional managers approve and direct all of the project work
Teams are dedicated and report directly to the project manager

Governance Arrangements.q: An organisation is defining its governance framework and debating whether the sponsor and project manager roles could be combined for smaller projects. In governance terms, why is it important that roles such as sponsor and project manager remain distinct?

So that the sponsor can focus on team performance
To avoid reporting to external stakeholders
So that the project manager can replace the sponsor if needed
To ensure the sponsor approves all team holidays

Governance Arrangements.q: A project board only meets after major problems have occurred. What is the most accurate criticism of this governance arrangement?
o: It improves efficiency by avoiding routine scrutiny
It prevents the project manager from managing the team
It gives too much authority to the sponsor
It is reactive rather than providing active oversight
Governance Arrangements.w: Governance should provide proactive oversight, not simply react after control has already failed.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager independently cancels a workstream because it appears to offer limited business value. What is the main problem?
o: They have reduced the overall complexity of the delivery programme
They have altered the project schedule without informing the delivery team
They have made a strategic value decision beyond normal delivery authority
They have shielded the sponsor from an unnecessary delivery decision
They have improved the efficiency of the governance approval process
Governance Arrangements.w: Cancelling work based on business value is a strategic decision that should involve the sponsor or governance body.

Governance Arrangements.q: A quick and inexpensive project is proposed to the board, but the benefits it would actually deliver to the organisation are very small. What does this indicate about the business case?
o: The project is automatically viable due to low cost
The project lacks sufficient justification despite efficiency
The project should proceed due to reduced risk
The project requires no further analysis
The project is strategically aligned by default

Governance Arrangements.q: A sponsor asks the project manager to decide whether the project should continue after the expected benefits have reduced significantly. What is the strongest governance issue?

The project manager should own all continuation decisions during delivery
The issue should only be reviewed after project closure
The project manager should continue if the schedule remains achievable
The sponsor is attempting to delegate strategic accountability inappropriately

Governance Arrangements.q: Following an incident where a serious problem was raised too late and to the wrong manager, a sponsor wants to make escalation more disciplined on future projects. Clarify who has authority to approve exceptions
Define tolerance thresholds at the start
Remove the project manager from decision-making
Delay reporting until a problem is irreversible

Governance Arrangements.q: A project board is concerned that spending on a capital project stays within authorised limits and wants to embed suitable controls in its governance arrangements. Which two practices help maintain financial control within governance limits?

Governance Arrangements.w: Regular budget reviews and clear delegation ensure spending stays within authorised limits.

n.3: Marketing efforts don’t enforce spending limits.

Governance Arrangements.q: Under pressure to hit an aggressive deadline in a matrix environment, a project manager stops routing decisions through the agreed governance and pushes ahead on his own authority. The sponsor is concerned about the consequences. What is the primary risk?
o: Slower decision-making across the wider stakeholder group
Additional administrative burden on the delivery team
Loss of control and misalignment with organisational objectives

Governance Arrangements.w: Users validate that the solution aligns with how it will be used in practice.

n.4: Funding is typically authorised by sponsors or boards.
n.3: Supplier management is handled by procurement roles.
n.1: The business case is created by the project manager or sponsor.
n.2: Tolerances are governed by the sponsor and project board.

Governance Arrangements.q: A local council deploys a citizen portal to improve transparency. Ensuring project objectives align with the council’s mission helped gain ______ approvals.
Governance Arrangements.w: Budgetary approvals are streamlined when projects align with mission and funding criteria.

n.4: Regulatory approvals relate to legal compliance, not mission alignment.
n.3: Holiday approvals pertain to time off, not project missions.
n.0: Team-member approvals aren’t formal governance approvals.
n.2: Decor approvals are unrelated to project objectives.

Governance Arrangements.q: A delivery team proposes three options to recover schedule slippage. The project board chooses the cheapest option without considering risk or benefit impact. What has most clearly failed?
Governance Arrangements.w: Governance decisions should consider balanced criteria, not cost alone.

Governance Arrangements.q: A sponsor is concerned that a large transformation project may drift away from the organisation's wider strategic priorities as delivery progresses. Which governance feature is most important for ensuring alignment between the project outcomes and the business strategy?
Governance Arrangements.w: Steering groups provide strategic oversight and help align project outcomes with business goals.

n.0: Risk registers manage uncertainty, not alignment.
n.4: Change control manages scope but not strategy alignment.
n.2: Lessons learned support future improvement.
n.3: Stand-ups are for operational updates, not strategic alignment.

Governance Arrangements.q: Throughout a project's life, responsibility for keeping the business case current and credible needs to sit clearly with the right people. Which TWO roles are most involved in maintaining the business case?
Governance Arrangements.w: Sponsor owns justification, project manager supports with delivery data.

Governance Arrangements.q: An engineering firm is concerned that placing staff into permanent, dedicated delivery teams could reduce how easily people draw on specialists based in other departments. Which of the following structures most likely limits access to shared functional expertise?
Governance Arrangements.w: Project-based teams may not have regular access to specialists from other departments.

n.4: Matrix structures allow sharing of specialists.
n.3: Functional structures centralise expertise.
n.1: Balanced matrix promotes collaboration between functions.
n.0: Hybrid models often maintain access to functional support.

Governance Arrangements.q: A governance board meets at a defined review point to consider whether a piece of work is still worth pursuing before releasing further funding. Which scenario best demonstrates the purpose of a business case in decision making?
o: Determining whether the project should start or continue
Selecting the best technical solution for delivery
Governance Arrangements.w: The business case supports key decisions on whether to initiate or continue a project.

Governance Arrangements.q: While managing a live project against agreed tolerances, a project manager is deciding which matters warrant raising above delivery level to a more senior figure. Which TWO situations should a project manager normally escalate to the sponsor?
o: A routine update to the issue log
A change that materially affects expected benefits
A delivery issue that threatens agreed tolerances
A completed task requiring no further decision
Governance Arrangements.w: Issues threatening tolerances or expected benefits require sponsor or governance attention.

Governance Arrangements.q: A consultant is classifying the structures used across a client's various delivery teams and needs to identify which arrangement is genuinely projectised rather than functional or matrix. Which scenario most strongly indicates a projectised structure?
o: Teams are assembled and report directly to the project manager
Project managers are given only very limited budget control
Governance decisions are made informally between senior department heads
Work is allocated according to wider departmental priorities
Resources report primarily to their own functional line managers
Governance Arrangements.w: Direct reporting to the project manager is a defining feature of projectised structures.

Governance Arrangements.q: Across an organisation, a well-established PMO enforces the use of consistent templates, mandatory reviews and standard reporting for every project. This arrangement is best described as an example of:
Governance Arrangements.w: Enforcing templates and reporting is part of establishing a robust governance framework.

n.0: Portfolio management is broader and strategic.
n.4: Alignment focuses on direction, not control.
n.3: Risk management is a component, not the structure itself.
n.2: Siloed delivery reflects separation, not structured oversight.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project is low risk and low cost but delivers limited benefit over a long timescale. What is the most likely conclusion?
o: The project may not be justified due to limited value
The project should proceed because its overall cost is low
The project should be prioritised ahead of higher-value work
The project can proceed with only minimal governance oversight
The project is clearly viable because its risk is low
Governance Arrangements.w: Limited benefits may not justify even low-cost, low-risk projects.

Governance Arrangements.q: Team members on a project are receiving instructions from both their department head and the project manager, leading to disputes over priorities. Which structure may result in this confusion over authority and dual reporting lines?
Governance Arrangements.w: Matrix structures often result in employees reporting to both functional and project managers.

n.2: Functional structures have clear single reporting lines.
n.0: Project structures have centralised authority with the project manager.
n.1: Agile teams are self-organising with clear role boundaries.
n.3: Product-based organisations typically follow a clear reporting structure.

Governance Arrangements.q: During a recovery review, the sponsor asks for options, consequences and recommendations from the project manager. What does this demonstrate?
o: The project team should now decide the recovery route
The project manager is replacing the governance board
The sponsor is interfering with delivery unnecessarily
The sponsor has transferred accountability to the project manager
The sponsor is using operational insight to support strategic decision-making
Governance Arrangements.w: The project manager provides delivery insight so the sponsor can make informed strategic decisions.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project coordinator is assembling the documentation that describes how their governance process operates day to day. They must choose genuine governance content for it. Which two items would you find in a governance process?
o: Social media plans and branding guidelines
Roles and responsibilities and reporting schedules
Governance Arrangements.w: Governance processes document who does what and when reports are due.

n.1: These are HR outputs, not governance process elements.
n.0: Menus and playlists aren’t governance related.
n.2: Briefings may occur, but snack inventory isn’t governance.
n.3: Marketing assets aren’t part of governance processes.

Governance Arrangements.q: On a product development initiative, the governance structure needs someone to represent the interests of those who will use the deliverables and confirm the outputs are fit for their needs. Which project role is typically responsible for ensuring that the project outputs meet user needs?
Governance Arrangements.w: The product owner ensures outputs align with stakeholder needs and priorities.

n.2: The sponsor ensures strategic fit but not detailed product requirements.
n.1: The Scrum Master ensures agile practices, not product validation.
n.3: Finance officers handle cost tracking, not product quality.
n.0: Secretaries support administration, not governance validation.

Governance Arrangements.q: A consultancy runs many concurrent client engagements and frequently needs to move specialists between them as demands shift week to week. Which organisational structure provides the most flexibility in allocating staff based on project need?
Governance Arrangements.w: Matrix structures enable cross-functional resource sharing based on changing project demands.

n.0: Functional structures allocate staff based on department, not project flexibility.
n.3: Project-based teams are dedicated and not easily reallocated.
n.1: Agile teams are cross-functional but often stable.
n.4: Hierarchical structures are slow to adapt resource needs.

Governance Arrangements.q: On an agile project, the steering group needs to stay informed about delivery direction and the relative importance of the work being undertaken. In agile governance, what is one way the product owner supports the steering group?
o: By tracking hours worked by developers
By communicating product progress and user priorities
By signing off the business case
Governance Arrangements.w: The product owner ensures the steering group is updated on value delivery and user needs.

n.0: Tracking hours is a delivery management task.
n.2: Financial control is sponsor or finance-owned.
n.4: Business cases are approved by governance bodies, not the PO.
n.1: Risk procedures are usually handled by the PM or governance officer.

Governance Arrangements.q: A sponsor approves a major change without asking the project manager for delivery impact analysis. What is the strongest criticism?
o: Delivery impacts are irrelevant if the sponsor approves the change
The project manager should have made the strategic decision alone
Strategic authority has been exercised without operational evidence
The team should have approved the change first
Governance Arrangements.w: Sponsors may make strategic decisions, but should use project manager input on delivery impacts.

Governance Arrangements.q: A sponsor wants to appoint a project manager who will hold complete accountability for the budget, schedule and the people delivering the work. Which organisational structure enables the project manager to have full control over budget, schedule, and resources?
Governance Arrangements.w: Project-based structures provide the project manager with maximum authority over all aspects of delivery.

n.2: Balanced matrix shares control with functional managers.
n.4: Functional structures centralise control with departmental heads.
n.3: Weak matrix structures limit project manager authority.
n.0: Strong matrix provides significant but not total control.

Governance Arrangements.q: As a project moves into its handover phase and the deliverables are transferred into operational use, the sponsor turns their attention to what matters most at their level. Which of the following would most likely be a project sponsor's concern during the handover phase?
o: Whether daily tasks are completed on time
Whether the team’s morale is high
Whether the project will deliver long-term benefits
Whether the risk log is up to date
Governance Arrangements.w: Sponsors are accountable for ensuring benefits realisation beyond the immediate project delivery.

n.0: Daily task tracking is managed by the PM.
n.1: Team morale is important but not a sponsor’s core concern.
n.3: Configuration management is a technical role.
n.4: Risk log updates are the project manager's responsibility.

Governance Arrangements.q: A time-critical initiative needs to make and act on delivery decisions quickly, without repeatedly seeking approval from separate departmental managers. In which type of organisational structure would you typically expect to see the most rapid project-level decisions?
Governance Arrangements.w: Project-based structures concentrate authority within the project team, enabling fast decisions.

n.2: Decisions in functional structures require departmental approval.
n.0: Balanced matrix shares decision-making, slowing speed.
n.4: Weak matrix prioritises functional leadership.
n.1: Hierarchical models tend to delay approval and decisions.

Governance Arrangements.q: A newly appointed project manager and an experienced project sponsor are agreeing how they will work together on a business-change project. The sponsor wants their respective governance accountabilities set out clearly from the outset. What differentiates the responsibilities of the project manager from those of the project sponsor?
o: The project manager signs off programme-level funding
The project manager approves the business case
The project manager manages delivery; the sponsor ensures justification
The project manager oversees the benefits review
The project manager defines organisational policy
Governance Arrangements.w: The PM ensures delivery of outputs; the sponsor ensures the project remains viable and justified.

n.1: The sponsor owns the business case.
n.3: Benefits are reviewed by the sponsor or benefits owner.
n.4: Policy is defined at the organisational level, not by the PM.
n.0: Programme-level funding is outside the PM’s remit.

Governance Arrangements.q: A regulated financial-services firm is establishing governance for a compliance-driven project and must ensure its work meets both corporate strategy and external rules. Complete the statement: effective governance ensures that project ______ are aligned with organisational objectives and regulatory requirements.
Governance Arrangements.w: Processes are the mechanisms through which governance ensures compliance and alignment.

n.4: Deliveries are outputs, not governance mechanisms.
n.0: Graphics are irrelevant to governance.
n.2: Colors have no bearing on governance.
n.1: Celebrations are cultural, not governance-related.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project is approaching closure and an assurance reviewer asks the project manager to evidence that all key decisions and approvals were properly recorded during delivery. Which governance document provides a record of all decisions made?
Governance Arrangements.w: The project log tracks decisions, actions, and approvals throughout the lifecycle.

n.1: Brochures are promotional, not governance records.
n.3: Holiday lists track time off, not project decisions.
n.4: Seating plans don’t document governance actions.
n.2: Design guides aren’t used for governance compliance.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager has been asked to deliver a change initiative using staff who continue to report to their departmental heads, and finds they must request people rather than direct them. In which organisational structure does the project manager typically have no direct authority over team members?
Governance Arrangements.w: In functional structures, project managers must request resources from functional heads and have little authority.

n.4: Project managers have full authority in this structure.
n.2: Strong matrix provides significant project manager authority.
n.3: Balanced matrix shares authority between PM and functional leads.
n.1: Hybrid varies but usually includes some project manager control.

Governance Arrangements.q: To improve delivery, a company restructures from a traditional functional set-up into a matrix in which staff now report to both their line managers and project managers. As the change beds in, the project office is asked to identify the main governance concern this introduces. What is the primary governance risk introduced?
Governance Arrangements.w: Matrix structures introduce dual authority, often creating ambiguity in accountability.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project moves smoothly from stage to stage, but the assumptions set out at initiation are never revisited even though the operating environment has since changed. What is the key risk?
Governance Arrangements.w: Failure to revisit assumptions leads to decisions based on outdated data.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project is failing due to unclear accountability between the sponsor and project manager. Decisions are delayed because neither takes ownership of escalation. Which interpretation best explains this failure?
o: The sponsor should only be involved at project closure and not during delivery
The project manager is responsible for all governance decisions regardless of structure
Team members are responsible for escalation decisions in most projects
Accountability has not been clearly defined between governance roles
External stakeholders should manage governance conflicts directly
Governance Arrangements.w: Failure to define accountability between sponsor and project manager leads to governance gaps and delays.

Governance Arrangements.q: A stakeholder new to project working asks how the two most senior project roles differ, given that both are heavily involved in the initiative's success. What distinguishes the responsibilities of a project sponsor compared to a project manager?
o: The sponsor delivers products; the manager signs off outputs
The sponsor manages day-to-day tasks; the manager manages benefits
The sponsor maintains the risk register; the manager handles benefit realisation
The sponsor defines team tasks; the manager approves the business case
The sponsor focuses on strategic alignment; the manager focuses on delivery

n.3: Task definition is the manager's responsibility, not the sponsor’s.
n.2: Risk management is usually managed by the PM with sponsor oversight.
n.0: Product delivery is coordinated by the PM; sign-offs are joint.

Governance Arrangements.q: A quality reviewer is assessing whether a project's governance arrangements are sound and is testing them against the hallmarks of good practice. One proposed trait clearly does not belong. Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of effective governance?
Governance Arrangements.w: Effective governance requires accountability, not its absence.

n.1: Decision paths ensure clarity in authority.
n.3: Reviews monitor adherence to governance.
n.2: Escalation routes are critical for issue resolution.
n.0: Procedures must be documented for consistency.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project is facing repeated delays due to lack of user input. Who should the project manager escalate this issue to?
Governance Arrangements.w: The sponsor can engage senior stakeholders and ensure user support is provided.

n.2: Product owners manage product decisions, not stakeholder engagement.
n.3: Scrum Masters facilitate teams, not resolve external user delays.
n.4: The secretary documents meetings but does not have decision authority.

Governance Arrangements.q: A newly appointed project manager is briefing colleagues on how governance responsibilities are shared with the sponsor throughout the project. Which TWO statements correctly describe the relationship between the sponsor and project manager?

The project manager provides delivery control and operational coordination
The sponsor should approve every operational decision
Both roles should avoid escalation to preserve speed
The sponsor provides strategic direction and owns business accountability
Governance Arrangements.w: The sponsor owns strategic direction and business accountability; the project manager controls delivery and coordination.

Governance Arrangements.q: On a delivery-phase IT project, the project manager grows uneasy about how closely the sponsor is engaging with the technical team. Which TWO situations indicate inappropriate sponsor involvement in operational delivery?
o: The sponsor challenges whether the business case remains valid
The sponsor gives daily instructions to technical team members
The sponsor reviews whether benefits remain achievable
The sponsor directly reallocates team tasks without the project manager
The sponsor approves a major funding decision
Governance Arrangements.w: Directly reallocating tasks and instructing team members are operational delivery activities that should sit with the project manager.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project delivers strong financial benefits but has an extended timescale that delays value realisation significantly. What is the key concern within the business case?
o: The governance structure is too complex
The delivery team is too small
The timing of benefits may reduce overall value
Governance Arrangements.w: Timescale affects when benefits are realised, which impacts overall value and viability.

Governance Arrangements.q: A new organisational change programme has just been authorised, and a colleague joining the team asks how the sponsor's role differs from the project manager's as the work moves into delivery. Which statement best distinguishes sponsor accountability from project manager responsibility?
o: The sponsor is only responsible for approving the final report
Both roles are accountable for the same decisions throughout the project
The sponsor manages outputs; the project manager owns benefits
The project manager owns business value once delivery begins
The sponsor owns strategic justification; the project manager manages delivery
Governance Arrangements.w: The sponsor is accountable for business justification and benefits, while the project manager is responsible for delivery.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project is technically on track, but senior stakeholders question whether it still supports organisational strategy. Who should primarily address this concern?
Governance Arrangements.w: Strategic alignment is primarily a sponsor-level responsibility.

Governance Arrangements.q: Midway through delivery, a project manager is deciding when the business case genuinely needs re-examining rather than being left unchanged. Which TWO situations should trigger a review of the business case?
Governance Arrangements.w: Changes in benefits or risk affect justification and require review.

Governance Arrangements.q: A newly formed project board is agreeing who owns which responsibilities, and the sponsor asks the project manager to confirm which duties sit with the sponsor role. Which TWO responsibilities are typically owned by the project sponsor?
Governance Arrangements.w: Sponsors oversee business justification and major decisions.

Governance Arrangements.q: An organisation is weighing a move to a fully projectised structure and wants to understand the governance effects before committing. It asks the PMO which results such a structure typically produces. Which TWO outcomes are most likely in a projectised organisation?
Governance Arrangements.w: Projectised structures provide clear accountability and strong authority.

Governance Arrangements.q: During project initiation, the board is clarifying the boundary between the sponsor's and the project manager's duties to avoid overlap. It asks which responsibilities properly belong to the project manager. Which TWO responsibilities are typically owned by the project manager?
Governance Arrangements.w: Project managers deliver outputs and coordinate teams.

Governance Arrangements.q: After a project suffered from confusion over who was responsible for what, a PMO is putting measures in place to prevent a recurrence on future work. It wants to focus on actions that genuinely improve role clarity. Which TWO actions help clarify roles and responsibilities in governance?
Governance Arrangements.w: Role clarity and escalation routes improve governance.

Governance Arrangements.q: After a programme office links each project's objectives to the corporate goals and communicates the connection to delivery teams, the sponsor lists the improvements she expects to see across the portfolio. Which of the following is NOT an expected outcome of this linkage?
Governance Arrangements.w: Linkage yields coordination, not uncoordinated efforts.

n.2: Alignment enhances decision clarity.
n.0: Resources get focused on strategic work.
n.3: Stakeholders back well-aligned projects.
n.4: Success is measured against strategic criteria.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager is maintaining a live business case and needs to know which developments genuinely warrant updating it rather than simply noting them. Which TWO factors should trigger an update to the business case?
Governance Arrangements.w: Changes in benefits or risk require updates.

Governance Arrangements.q: Following repeated disputes over authority between project and functional managers, a governance board wants to introduce mechanisms that reduce such conflict in its matrix organisation. Which TWO governance mechanisms help mitigate authority conflicts in matrix structures?
Governance Arrangements.w: Clear escalation and role clarity reduce conflict.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager compiles a benefits map for a new initiative and identifies a range of benefits, but does not check them against the organisation's strategic goals or corporate objectives. If this approach continues unchallenged, what is the principal risk to the project?
o: The project manager will lose authority
The benefits may not deliver meaningful value
The project will exceed its timeline
The team will not complete tasks
Governance Arrangements.w: Benefits must align with strategy to deliver meaningful value.

Governance Arrangements.q: Under intense pressure to hit deadlines, a project manager concentrates solely on producing the agreed outputs and rarely refers back to the business case. What is the primary risk of working this way?
o: Loss of alignment with business value
Governance Arrangements.w: Ignoring the business case risks delivering outputs that do not provide value.

Governance Arrangements.q: A senior executive has agreed to take on a governance role for a major project and wants to understand what will be expected of them at that level. The responsibilities of a project sponsor typically include:

Providing resources, championing the project, and ensuring alignment with strategy
Maintaining the issue log, risk register, and daily timesheets
Writing detailed test cases, quality checklists, and acceptance criteria
Operating the financial software and reconciling costs each day

n.0: These are tasks typically done by agile team roles like the Scrum Master.
n.3: These are quality assurance tasks, not sponsor duties.
n.4: This is a task for project support or administrators.
n.2: The issue log is maintained by the project manager or support roles.

Governance Arrangements.q: A sponsor asks the project manager to continue despite evidence that benefits are no longer achievable. Which governance principle is being undermined?
Governance Arrangements.w: Governance must ensure the project remains justified and aligned with expected benefits.

Governance Arrangements.q: An organisation is establishing clear governance for a change programme and wants to be explicit about accountability once the project outputs are handed over into operational use. Considering how benefits are owned and realised, which TWO roles are most responsible for ensuring the intended benefits are actually achieved?
Governance Arrangements.w: Sponsors and business owners are responsible for benefits realisation.

Governance Arrangements.q: A capable project team finds itself waiting for sign-off on routine, low-value tasks because approvals must always pass upward, and delivery is slipping as a result. What is the most likely governance issue?

Governance Arrangements.w: Poor delegation leads to unnecessary escalation and delays.

Governance Arrangements.q: During delivery of a system-integration project, a serious disagreement develops between the project team and a group of external users over acceptance criteria, and it cannot be settled at working level. n.1: Support officers facilitate admin, not conflict resolution.
n.4: Finance managers handle cost reporting, not team dynamics.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project to introduce a new customer-service system is delivered on time and to specification, and the outputs are formally accepted. What does this situation most clearly indicate?

Governance Arrangements.q: A project delivers all outputs successfully, but no mechanism exists to track whether expected benefits are realised. What is the primary failure?
o: Benefits management has not been defined or implemented
The governance structure is too complex
The project manager has not controlled delivery effectively
Governance Arrangements.w: Benefits must be tracked and managed beyond delivery; otherwise value cannot be confirmed.

Governance Arrangements.q: A newly appointed project manager is briefed on how governance is expected to operate across the organisation's portfolio, and is given a list of characteristics associated with well-controlled projects. Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of strong project governance?
Governance Arrangements.w: Strong governance avoids ad hoc decisions by enforcing structure and consistency.

n.1: Strong governance clarifies all roles.
n.4: Escalation paths are clearly defined.
n.2: Reporting lines are essential for oversight.
n.0: Stage boundaries mark progress points.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager identifies that a proposed change would improve delivery efficiency but reduce expected business benefits. What should they do?

Ask the project team to vote on whether the change is acceptable
Implement it quietly if the delivery baseline improves
Reject the change because benefits are outside the project manager's role

Governance Arrangements.q: A governance reviewer observes that on several projects the sponsor routinely steps in to make operational, day-to-day decisions rather than leaving them to the project manager. Governance Arrangements.q: A sponsor is highly engaged in benefits, stakeholder commitment and funding, but avoids daily delivery decisions. What is the best assessment?

Governance Arrangements.q: A software project is being delivered using an agile approach, and the team needs someone to decide what functionality matters most and in what order it should be built. Which of the following is a primary responsibility of the product owner?

n.2: Team management is the role of the project manager.
n.4: The sponsor owns the business case, not the product owner.
n.0: Procurement is managed by specialised roles or the PM.
n.3: Regulatory compliance is typically a shared or delegated responsibility.

Governance Arrangements.q: An organisation is deciding what will set the benchmarks and the authority required to accept its project deliverables under the governance arrangements. Complete the statement: governance ________ define the criteria and authority for accepting project deliverables.

The project will become easier to govern

Governance Arrangements.q: A proposed solution would deliver benefits soon after go-live but would then carry noticeably higher operational costs for years afterwards. What should the business case take into account?

The frequency of progress reporting to the sponsor
The balance between short-term benefits and long-term costs

Governance Arrangements.q: On a project where the sponsor's, project manager's and team's roles were never clearly defined, the board is now reviewing the problems that have emerged during delivery. Which TWO governance failures are most likely when roles are poorly defined?

Governance Arrangements.q: Your project is halfway through its lifecycle and requires additional funding. According to governance limits, you must seek _______ from the project board.

n.3: Social events are outside governance scope.

Governance Arrangements.q: A project manager working within a matrix organisation finds that decisions about who works on the project, and on what, are not theirs alone. In a matrix structure, who typically has shared authority over resources and task allocation?

n.3: Administrators support projects but don’t control resources.
n.0: The PMO oversees standards, not daily task control.
n.4: Team members do not hold authority over resource allocation.

Governance Arrangements.q: An international aid project spanning many partners needs consistent oversight, and the sponsor is reviewing proposed measures to strengthen its governance. One suggestion would actually weaken it. Which of the following would NOT improve governance in this scenario?

n.0: Escalation paths ensure issues can be raised effectively.

Governance Arrangements.q: As a project passes key milestones, both the sponsor and the project manager are expected to play a part in checking that the investment still stacks up. Which activity is typically shared between the project sponsor and project manager?
