n.2: Regulatory changes can impact assumptions.
n.4: Budget variances affect viability.
n.0: Quality failures can change cost/benefit forecasts.

Business Case.q: A startup assesses its lack of brand recognition against a competitor’s strong positioning. Which SWOT category does the startup’s weakness belong to?
Business Case.w: Lack of brand recognition is an internal weakness in SWOT.

n.2: Threats are external challenges, not internal issues.
n.0: Opportunities are external positive factors.
n.4: Strengths are internal positives.
n.1: Ambiguity is a VUCA element, not SWOT.

Business Case.q: When a project team revisits the business case during a scheduled review, certain core components almost always need refreshing to reflect the latest position. Which TWO elements of the business case are typically updated during such a review?
Business Case.w: Cost forecasts and benefit estimates must reflect the latest information.

n.3: Office layout is unrelated to the business case.
n.2: Risk and communication plans are separate governance documents.
n.4: Team charters and supplier lists aren’t core business case elements.
n.0: Schedules and test cases belong to planning and execution artifacts.

Business Case.q: A project manager preparing a business case for a new consumer product wants to understand how much disposable income potential customers have and how their spending patterns and lifestyles are changing. Which pair of PESTLE factors should be examined to address both of these considerations?
Business Case.w: Economic covers income; Social covers spending behaviours.

n.2: Political/Economic omit social spending context.
n.0: Technological does not cover spending habits.
n.1: Environmental/Legal irrelevant here.
n.3: Strengths/Weaknesses are SWOT terms.

Business Case.q: A project manager is warning the team about the consequences of neglecting to assess the impact of emerging changes on the business case. Complete the statement: failing to review impacts can lead to ______ deviations going unnoticed.
Business Case.w: Significant deviations threaten project success if not detected early.

n.2: Minor deviations may also matter, but the focus is on significant ones.
n.4: Irrelevant deviations by definition don’t matter.
n.0: Planned deviations are accounted for.

Business Case.q: Following a major approved change to a live project, the project manager must bring the business case up to date so it still reflects reality. Which TWO of the following actions are essential when carrying out this update?

n.3: Office layout and emails are logistical, not business case elements.

Business Case.q: A project sponsor wants a PESTLE analysis to explore the level of market demand for a new service and how income is distributed across the target population. Which pair of PESTLE factors should the team draw on to examine both of these aspects?
Business Case.w: Economic covers demand/income; Social covers demographics.

n.4: Uncertainty/Ambiguity are VUCA terms.

Business Case.q: An organisation's executive board meets each quarter to confirm that its portfolio of projects still represents a worthwhile investment and remains justified. When judging whether a given project is still viable, against what should the board compare its progress?

Business Case.q: Three months into delivery, monitoring reveals that the benefits actually being realised are trailing well behind the levels set out in the plan. Given this growing gap between planned and actual benefits, what should the project sponsor do?

n.0: Scope expansion may worsen issues.

Business Case.q: A project manager is coaching a colleague on the VUCA model as a way of characterising a turbulent operating environment. When listing the four elements that make up the framework, which of the following terms does NOT belong to VUCA?

Business Case.q: A sponsor wants assurance that variances from plan will be picked up promptly rather than surfacing too late to act on. Complete the statement: effective ______ of the business case ensures early detection of variances.

n.1: Delegation isn’t relevant to variance detection.

Business Case.q: A project team is trying to forecast future demand from a set of market figures that can be read in several conflicting ways, leaving members unable to agree on what the data actually means. Which VUCA element best characterises the difficulty they are facing?
Business Case.w: Ambiguity captures unclear or incomplete information.

n.0: Uncertainty is unpredictability.

Business Case.q: A fast-growing tech startup is preparing to enter an unfamiliar, heavily regulated overseas market where the rules and likely outcomes remain unclear. Using VUCA, which element should the startup first assess?
Business Case.w: Uncertainty applies when rules or outcomes are unclear.

n.0: Complexity is about interdependencies.

Business Case.q: A developer preparing the business case for a renewable energy scheme must weigh both its sustainability impact and the government incentives that could support it. Which pair of PESTLE factors should this project analyse most closely?

Business Case.q: A project manager completes a scheduled review of the business case at a stage boundary and must record for governance what the review has produced. Which pair of outputs would typically result from a regular business case review?

Business Case.q: Midway through a project the sponsor requests a structured review to confirm the business case remains viable. As the project manager prepares the session, which pair of activities would typically take place during a business case review?

Business Case.q: A project manager is drawing up the agenda for a business case review meeting with the sponsor and steering group. Checking the proposed items, which one is NOT typically part of a business case review meeting?

Business Case.q: A project manager finds that changing market conditions have materially altered the expected returns set out in the business case, and the revised justification needs formal sign-off before it can be adopted. Resource levelling should only affect non-critical tasks
The levelling process was incorrectly applied

n.0: They may need adjustment under constraints.

Allocate randomly to ensure a fair distribution
Allocate based on the duration of each task
Allocate equally across all remaining project tasks
Allocate based on risk exposure and potential impact

n.0: Pressure is not a valid planning criterion.

Evenly distribute limited resources across all tasks
Increase overall project duration to match resource availability
Allocate resources based on initial estimates and adjust later

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: At the outset of planning a delivery project, a project manager works to surface limitations on resources, funding and time as early as possible. In resource planning, what is the main purpose of identifying constraints early?

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: A project manager must choose between using highly skilled but limited resources or less skilled but available resources. What is the most appropriate consideration?
